questions.name: documentation
questions.instructions:
Is `page` documentation for software: a reference page, manual, specification or guide to how the software works?

True if: The page explains how the software works, such as an API or configuration reference, a manual, a specification or a user guide.
False if: The page is a blog post or article, a forum or Q&A thread, an issue or discussion, a marketing page, or a page with almost no content.

questions.name: makers
questions.instructions:
Is `page` published by the makers of the software that `docs_question` asks about?

True if: The page is on the project's or vendor's own documentation site, website or source repository.
False if: The page is written by someone else: a blog, tutorial site, Q&A answer, forum, news article or a copy of the documentation hosted elsewhere.

questions.name: names_release
questions.instructions:
Does `docs_question` name a specific version or release of the software it asks about?

True if: The question gives a version number or a named release, such as "3.12", "v5", "version 2" or "the 2024 edition".
False if: The question names the software without any version or release.

questions.name: other_release
questions.instructions:
Does `page` document a different version or release than the one `docs_question` names?

True if: The page's title, address or text shows a version or release other than the one the question names.
False if: The page shows the version the question names, or shows no version at all.

choices.description: Reference documentation: an API, command, configuration or language reference, a manual page or a specification.
A guide or tutorial in a documentation set that walks through how to do something.
A blog post, news item or article written by a person or company.
A forum thread or a question-and-answer page such as Stack Overflow.
An issue, pull request or discussion thread in a code hosting site.
A source code file or a repository file listing.
A marketing, product or landing page.
